subject: Data Science
topic: Deep Learning in Data Science/Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) in Image Analysis

items.question: How do convolutional layers and fully connected layers work together in a CNN?
items.answer: Convolutional layers perform spatial convolutions to extract features from the input image, while fully connected layers classify the output into predefined classes.

items.question: What is the difference between max pooling and average pooling?
items.answer: Max pooling reduces spatial dimensions by taking the maximum value across each region, whereas average pooling takes the mean value.

items.question: In what ways can CNNs be used for image segmentation tasks?
items.answer: CNNs are used for image segmentation through architectures such as U-Net and Convolutional Autoencoders (CAE), which perform pixel-wise classification to separate objects from the background.

items.question: How does batch normalization improve training stability in deep neural networks?
items.answer: Batch normalization normalizes input data for each layer, reducing the effect of internal covariate shift and improving training stability by speeding up convergence.

items.question: Can CNNs be combined with Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) to create a hybrid architecture?
items.answer: Yes, CNNs can be combined with RNNs to create hybrid architectures for sequential data such as videos or text images, allowing the network to model temporal relationships.
